note: Ratchet for raw literal padding/margin/gap/border-radius declarations in src/**/*.css - see scripts/check-spacing-ratchet.mjs. Total and per-file counts below are inherited technical debt: a --space-* and --radius-* token scale exists (src/styles/tokens/primitives.css) but the vast majority of spacing/radius declarations across the app predate it and still use raw px/rem/%/clamp()/calc() literals. Unlike the hex and rgb()/hsl() colour ratchets, migrating these is out of scope here - rounding a spacing value to the nearest token step can visibly shift a real shipped layout, and there is no visual-regression tooling in place to catch that. This ratchet is already at its ceiling: no new raw literals are permitted anywhere, including in the files listed below - lower a file's count as it gets migrated (incrementally, separately, and reviewed with screenshots), never raise it, and do not add new entries for files that aren't already listed.
policy: A declaration's value is compliant only if every numeric magnitude in it ultimately comes from a var(--space-*) or var(--radius-*) reference (directly, or composed via calc()/clamp() alongside one of those vars). Bare `0`, `auto`, `inherit`, `initial`, and `unset` are always compliant since they carry no scale magnitude - they are excluded from the count. Everything else - a raw literal on its own (12px, 0.5rem, 999px), inside clamp()/calc() with no var() at all, or mixed with a token reference in the same shorthand (10px var(--space-4)) - counts as non-compliant. No other exceptions are documented: border-radius: 999px is common for pills/avatars in this codebase (49 uses), but the project already has an exact --radius-full: 999px token for that value, so it is inherited debt to migrate, not a permanent exception; border-radius: 50% does not currently appear in src/**/*.css. New component work must use var(--space-*)/var(--radius-*) instead of a raw literal. If a new use is genuinely unavoidable, it must be added to the relevant file's count below in the same commit, with a comment in the CSS explaining why.
